name: Introduction and overview — Fletcher-class Destroyer — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Fletcher-class Destroyer
description: Introduction and overview of the Fletcher-class Destroyer: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Fletcher class was the U.S. Navy's standard World War II destroyer: 175 built, more than any other U.S. destroyer class. At 376 feet with five 5-inch guns and ten torpedo tubes, Fletchers fought in every Pacific campaign. Nineteen were lost in the war; survivors served into the 1970s with allied navies. Baseline facts: U.S. WWII destroyer class; 175 built; 376 ft; five 5-inch guns; Pacific war workhorse..

description: Comparison with contemporaries of the Fletcher-class Destroyer: How the class compared with rival navies' ships. The Fletcher class was the U.S. Navy's standard World War II destroyer: 175 built, more than any other U.S. destroyer class. At 376 feet with five 5-inch guns and ten torpedo tubes, Fletchers fought in every Pacific campaign. Nineteen were lost in the war; survivors served into the 1970s with allied navies. Baseline facts: U.S. WWII destroyer class; 175 built; 376 ft; five 5-inch guns; Pacific war workhorse..
